summary: Kalpana K. Sheth is an Indologist who completed her doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani. She held a post at the L.D. Institute of Indology.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Ösel Ling, served as Vajra Master at Palpung, became abbot of Changchub Choeling Monastery in 1957, and founded Samdrup Thargye Ling in 1965.
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar worked in Indology and Sinology and studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as Emeritus Professor at the University of Windsor, attested in 2002.
Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She served at Stony Brook University as director, attested in 2007, and as Professor Emerita, attested in 2026.

Kamala Tiyavanich specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Brown University from around 1968 to 1970, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.

Kameshwar Nath Mishra is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who studied under Ram Chandra Dwivedi. He held posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–2001) and was a visiting research scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Charles University. He held posts at the Czech Oriental Institute, Charles University, University of Chicago, Heidelberg University, Collège de France, and Utrecht University.

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, the University of the Punjab, the University of Calcutta, and Michigan State University (~1946–1949). She later held posts at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi studied under Kshetreśachandra Chattopadhyaya in Indology and religious studies. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang (born 1965) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Su Bai. He has served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (born 1932) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and earned his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, later becoming a Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta.
Kanchu Onoue is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a teacher at Hikone Higashi High School, attested in 1963, and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin, attested in 1976.

Kang-nam Oh is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974) and earned his doctorate under Yün-hua Jan. He held an attested post at the University of Regina from 1990 to 1998.
Kang-yuan Sung is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed an MA at the University of Calgary, studying under Anthony W. Barber, Anne Moore, and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a Buddhist studies and history/archaeology scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris. He later served as a non-regular staff member at Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura (born 1944) is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Rissho University, including as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).

Kanoko Tanaka is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Acharya Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University, attested in 2001.
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (attested 1962). He held a post as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1962.
